Diversity-Area Relationship (DAR)

Source: R/sar.R
dar.Rd

Diversity against cumulative area along a spatial accumulation, for Hill numbers (Ma 2018) or for any curve spacc computes: species richness, phylogenetic and functional metrics, redundancy.

Usage

dar(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
dar(
  x,
  coords,
  q = c(0, 1, 2),
  n_seeds = 50L,
  method = "knn",
  area_method = c("convex_hull", "voronoi", "count"),
  distance = c("euclidean", "haversine"),
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  progress = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  focal_points = NULL,
  focal_domain = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'spacc'
dar(x, area_method = c("convex_hull", "voronoi", "count"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'spacc_hill'
dar(x, area_method = c("convex_hull", "voronoi", "count"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'spacc_phylo'
dar(x, area_method = c("convex_hull", "voronoi", "count"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'spacc_func'
dar(x, area_method = c("convex_hull", "voronoi", "count"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'spacc_redundancy'
dar(x, area_method = c("convex_hull", "voronoi", "count"), ...)

Arguments

x

A site-by-species matrix (abundance data recommended), or a curve object: spacc, spacc_hill, spacc_phylo, spacc_func or spacc_redundancy. A matrix is first passed to spaccHill() with q.

...

Arguments passed to methods.

coords

A data.frame with columns x and y, or a spacc_dist object (matrix input only).

q

Numeric vector. Diversity orders (matrix input only). Default c(0, 1, 2).

n_seeds

Integer. Number of random starting points. Default 50.

method

Character. Accumulation method: "knn" or "nn_walk".

area_method

Character. How to measure the area covered by the first k sites of an order: "convex_hull" (area of their convex hull, 0 until three sites span a polygon), "voronoi" (summed area of their Voronoi cells within the bounding box of all sites) or "count" (number of sites). Areas are in squared coordinate units. Default "convex_hull".

distance

Character. Distance method. Default "euclidean".

parallel

Logical. Use parallel processing? Default TRUE.

n_cores

Integer. Number of cores.

progress

Logical. Show progress? Default TRUE.

seed

Integer. Random seed.

focal_points

Optional focal points for method = "knn". See spacc().

focal_domain

Optional polygonal focal domain. See spacc().

Value

An object of class spacc_dar containing:

curves

Named list of diversity curves (n_seeds x n_sites), one per metric or order

metric

Names of the curves

area

Matrix of cumulative areas (n_seeds x n_sites)

power_law

Data frame with the power-law fit \(D = c A^z\) of each mean curve (metric, c, z)

q

Diversity orders for Hill-number input, else NULL

area_method

Method used for area estimation

source

Class of the curve object the DAR was built from

object

That curve object

Details

The DAR (Ma, 2018) generalizes the SAR by replacing species richness (q=0) with Hill numbers of any order. This reveals how different facets of diversity scale with area:

  • q=0 (richness) recovers the classic SAR

  • q=1 (Shannon) shows how common species diversity scales

  • q=2 (Simpson) shows how dominant species diversity scales

The area is accumulated along the same site orders as the diversity curve, so any curve object gives its own diversity-area relationship: functional richness, dispersion and other facets can scale with area differently from richness (Dias et al. 2025). The power-law exponent z is the slope of log mean diversity against log mean area over the steps where both are positive.

References

Ma, Z.S. (2018). DAR (diversity-area relationship): extending classic SAR for biodiversity and biogeography analyses. Ecology and Evolution, 8, 10023-10038.

Arrhenius, O. (1921). Species and area. Journal of Ecology, 9, 95-99.

Dias, R.A., Bastazini, V.A.G., Gianuca, A.T. & Matthews, T.J. (2025). The spatial scaling of multiple dimensions of functional diversity in habitat islands. Functional Ecology. doi:10.1111/1365-2435.70158

See also

spaccHill(), spaccFunc(), spaccPhylo(), extrapolate()

Examples

# \donttest{
coords <- data.frame(x = runif(50), y = runif(50))
species <- matrix(rpois(50 * 30, 2), nrow = 50)

d <- dar(species, coords, q = c(0, 1, 2))
plot(d)

traits <- matrix(rnorm(30 * 2), nrow = 30)
func <- spaccFunc(species, coords, traits, metric = c("fdis", "fric"))
dar(func)
# }
